data.title: A rejection issued without human involvement is regulated in the EU (GDPR Art. 22)
data.summary: Under EU data protection law a person has the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them. Recital 71 names the case directly: "automatic refusal of an online credit application or e-recruiting practices without any human intervention", and states the person should have "the right to obtain human intervention, to express his or her point of view, to obtain an explanation of the decision reached after such assessment and to challenge the decision". The distinction the regulation turns on is whether a human was involved at all — the same line the US applicant rules draw, reached from the opposite direction: one governs who must be counted, this one governs what the person may demand. It binds processing in the EU, it says nothing about decisions a human did make, and a rejection preceded by genuine human review falls outside it.
